I have always been a busy person, but I was always able to handle my day-to-day life without this kind of constant, overwhelming anxiety.\n\nDoctor: Did your worry and tension start soon after your husband’s illness and caregiving stress, and have they stayed mainly linked to that stressor? I haven't really adjusted to the situation at all; instead, these feelings have been continuous and the stress of managing his care alongside my other commitments has just remained completely overwhelming.\n\nDoctor: Have your symptoms mostly improved once you adjusted to your husband’s illness, or have they continued for more than 6 months after the stressor started even without much change in the situation?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't improved at all and have continued constantly for about seven months now. Ever since my husband's health problems settled into a long-term routine, I've been stuck in this state of worry and tension without any relief.\n\nDoctor: Have your symptoms lasted longer than 6 months after the stressful situation started, or did they begin to ease once you had more time to adjust?\n\nPatient: Yes, they have lasted for about seven months now and haven't eased up at all. They started right around the time my husband's health problems became a long-term routine, and the worry and tension have just been constant ever since.\n\nDoctor: Have you been feeling this level of excessive worry and tension for most days over the past 6 months or longer, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?\n\nPatient: Yes, I’ve been feeling this way almost every single day for about seven months now. Even on quiet days when there are no medical appointments or immediate problems to deal with, my mind still races with \"what-ifs\" and my body remains incredibly tight and on edge.\n\nDoctor: Before your husband’s illness began, did you ever have a long period of excessive worry about many different things for 6 months or more, or is this the first time you’ve had symptoms like this?\n\nPatient: No, this is definitely the first time I have ever struggled with symptoms like this. Before my husband's illness, I never experienced this level of constant, overwhelming worry in my life."

What brings you in today?\n\nPatient: I feel like I’m constantly bracing myself—my whole body stays tight all day from worrying about my husband and everything I’m juggling. My primary care doctor actually noticed how incredibly tense I was during a routine visit recently and suggested I seek some help. It has just become so overwhelming to manage it all.\n\nDoctor: Did these worries and tension start after a specific stressful event or change in your life, or have they been going on for a long time without one clear trigger?\n\nPatient: Yes, it really started about seven months ago. I really didn't have this level of constant anxiety or tension before his illness.\n\nDoctor: Have your worries and tension gradually improved at all as you’ve adjusted to your husband’s illness, or have they stayed about the same or gotten worse over time?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't improved at all—they've actually gotten worse and more overwhelming over the last seven months. Ever since his health routine became a long-term thing, the constant worry has just taken over my life. It finally got to the point where it was too much to handle, which is why I realized I needed to seek help.\n\nDoctor: Have your symptoms been causing problems mainly because of this specific stressor, or do you also have excessive worry that feels hard to control even when you are not thinking about your husband or caregiving?\n\nPatient: Yes, the worry feels completely out of my control and spreads to other things, like whether I'm letting people down at the art center or if we'll have enough money for his medicines. Even when I try to relax, read, or go to my book club, these \"what-ifs\" just barge right in and I can't seem to stop them.\n\nDoctor: Have you also been having trouble sleeping, feeling restless, getting fatigued easily, or having muscle tension most days because of the worry?\n\nPatient: While I can sleep a full night, I still wake up feeling completely wrung out and fatigued, as if I'm constantly moving through molasses. I never experienced this kind of ongoing, constant anxiety and physical tension before his illness and my caregiving responsibilities began.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or panic that peak within minutes, with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest tightness, or feeling like something terrible is about to happen?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never had sudden, overwhelming spikes of panic like that. My anxiety is more of a constant, lingering worry and physical tension that stays with me all day long.\n\nDoctor: Over the past seven months, have you been feeling down or hopeless most days, or is the main problem the worry and tension?\n\nPatient: The main problem is definitely the constant worry and physical tension, rather than feeling down or hopeless. While the strain has exhausted me and taken the joy out of my activities, the real driving force is the non-stop worrying about my husband and my commitments. It just keeps my body feeling completely tight, braced, and on edge all day long.\n\nDoctor: Did these symptoms begin within about 3 months of your husband’s diagnosis and caregiving stress, and are they mainly tied to that stressor? It feels like every little hiccup is going to snowball into some terrible disaster.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least 6 months before this where you were worrying excessively about many different things most days, even without a major stressor like your husband’s illness?\n\nPatient: No, I don't recall ever having a period of worry like this in the past before my husband's health problems started. I have always been a busy person, but I was always able to handle my day-to-day life without this kind of constant, overwhelming anxiety.\n\nDoctor: Did your worry and tension start soon after your husband’s illness and caregiving stress, and have they stayed mainly linked to that stressor? Or did they continue for a long time after you had adjusted to the situation?\n\nPatient: Yes, they started about seven months ago, shortly after my husband's health issues settled into a long-term routine. I haven't really adjusted to the situation at all; instead, these feelings have been continuous and the stress of managing his care alongside my other commitments has just remained completely overwhelming.\n\nDoctor: Have your symptoms mostly improved once you adjusted to your husband’s illness, or have they continued for more than 6 months after the stressor started even without much change in the situation?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't improved at all and have continued constantly for about seven months now. Ever since my husband's health problems settled into a long-term routine, I've been stuck in this state of worry and tension without any relief.\n\nDoctor: Have your symptoms lasted longer than 6 months after the stressful situation started, or did they begin to ease once you had more time to adjust?\n\nPatient: Yes, they have lasted for about seven months now and haven't eased up at all. They started right around the time my husband's health problems became a long-term routine, and the worry and tension have just been constant ever since.\n\nDoctor: Have you been feeling this level of excessive worry and tension for most days over the past 6 months or longer, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?\n\nPatient: Yes, I’ve been feeling this way almost every single day for about seven months now. Even on quiet days when there are no medical appointments or immediate problems to deal with, my mind still races with \"what-ifs\" and my body remains incredibly tight and on edge.\n\nDoctor: Before your husband’s illness began, did you ever have a long period of excessive worry about many different things for 6 months or more, or is this the first time you’ve had symptoms like this?\n\nPatient: No, this is definitely the first time I have ever struggled with symptoms like this. Before my husband's illness, I never experienced this level of constant, overwhelming worry in my life.\n\nDoctor: Have these worries and physical tension been mainly a response to your husband’s illness and caregiving stress, or do they continue even when you’re not dealing with that stressor and feel out of proportion to it?\n\nPatient: While my husband's illness definitely triggered this, the worry and physical tension have taken on a life of their own now. Even when I'm away from caregiving, like trying to relax at my book club, I just can't turn it off and my mind constantly drifts to worst-case scenarios. It feels completely out of proportion because I'm also constantly worrying about other things, like our finances and letting people down at the art center.\n\nDoctor: Since your husband’s illness and caregiving situation began, have your symptoms mostly been tied to that stressor and gradually eased as you adjusted, or have they continued for more than 6 months after the stressor started and felt out of proportion to it?\n\nPatient: They definitely haven't eased up; they have been going on continuously for about seven months now. Instead of adjusting to my caregiving role, the constant worrying and physical tension have persisted and feel completely overwhelming and out of proportion.\n\nDoctor: Have these symptoms caused you significant problems in work, caregiving, or social activities, and do they seem clearly tied to the stress of your husband’s illness rather than a more general ongoing anxiety pattern?"
